subject: Post-call: Performance / SLO qualification follow-up (context window & latency)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@finco.com>, Alex Li <alex.li@finco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance / SLO qualification follow-up (context window & latency)

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we can scope a validation plan: 

Call summary (short):
- Use case: Agent-assist and automated response generation in FinCo's customer support flows.
- Key non-functional asks: tight latency SLOs, predictable throughput and streaming support for partial responses.
- Model surface: FinCo will evaluate a 16k-context model for longer threads, but many calls will be ~1k token inputs.

Clarifications / items we discussed:
1) Context window / token limits:
   - Typical prompt size: ~1,000 tokens (customer history + instruction).
   - Max input (expected): up to 16,384 tokens (16k) in peak cases.
   - Expected output: typically 200-600 tokens, max ~1,000 tokens.
2) Latency SLO targets (FinCo stated goals):
   - For typical prompts (~1k input + 300 output): p95 end-to-end generation <= 800 ms.
   - For heavy contexts (16k input + 1k output): p95 <= 2,000 ms (soft).
   - Streaming required: clients must see first token within 150-250 ms for perceived latency.
3) Throughput / concurrency:
   - Steady-state: ~500 requests/min (~8.3 rps).
   - Peak bursts: up to 2,000 requests/min (~33.3 rps) for short windows.
   - Concurrent active sessions: ~40-100 (concurrency ~50 typical).
4) Other constraints:
   - All inference must run in a dedicated VPC (private deployment) per customer data rules.
   - Audit logs and token-level cost reporting required for internal chargebacks.

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- We will run a small qualification test: 1) baseline latency test for typical prompts (1k/300), 2) stress test for concurrency and burst, and 3) heavy-context run for 16k inputs with streaming turned on.
- Deliverables: short report (latency percentiles, throughput curves, CPU/GPU utilization traces) + recommended configuration (batching, quantization, routing).
- What we need from you: a sample set of payloads (anonymized) that reflect the 1k and 16k cases, and confirmation of exact p95 SLOs you want us to validate and sign off on.

Can you drop the example payloads and your formal SLO matrix into the Jira ticket (FIN-1223) or reply here? Once we have that, Neha (SE) and I will schedule the validation window — suggest a 2-hour run during a representative afternoon slot next week.

Attachments: none from our side for this email.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

From: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Li <alex.li@finco.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance / SLO qualification follow-up (context window & latency)

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap. We scoped internally and attached our initial SLO requirements and a couple example payloads (anonymized). A few quick clarifications inline: 

- SLO numbers: we can be flexible but prefer p95 <= 700 ms for the 1k case and p95 <= 1,800 ms for the 16k heavy case. The 2,000 ms number you mentioned is acceptable as a fallback.
- Streaming: yes — first-byte times matter. We'd like first token streamed within 200 ms under the 1k case. For heavy contexts, initial token within 400 ms is acceptable so long as subsequent token throughput is steady.
- Throughput: the 2,000 requests/min peak is accurate for marketing spikes; the steady 500/min is our baseline.
- Concurrency: 50 concurrent active sessions is a realistic operational target.

We've attached: FinCo_SLO_requirements.pdf and example_payloads.json (anonymized). The Jira FIN-1223 has links to the ops runbook.

On schedule: we can provide a validation window next Wed (2027-04-21) 1-4pm PT — if that works for you and Neha.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Johnson
Head of Digital Ops | FinCo
FinCo Inc.

Attachments:
- FinCo_SLO_requirements.pdf (PDF, 210 KB)
- example_payloads.json (JSON, 45 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@finco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Alex Li <alex.li@finco.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance / SLO qualification follow-up (context window & latency)

Hi Sarah,

Perfect, thanks for the attachments and the clarifications. Quick notes: 

- Neha will take point on the qualification run — she'll define the workload mix (1k typical vs 16k heavy) and share the exact load generator script.
- We'll aim for the Wed 1-4pm PT window; I'll send a calendar invite with the Zoom link and expected run deck.
- A couple of technical asks so our validation maps to your production topology:
   * Can you confirm whether the 16k cases include the full customer history or are you planning to trim/summary on the client side? That affects KV cacheability and latency significantly.
   * Are you running strict per-user rate limits in front of the model (e.g., 1 request/sec/user)? If so, please share expected token-per-minute per user so we can simulate realistic concurrency.

Next deliverables from Redwood by Tue EOD: proposed test plan + pass/fail criteria tied to the p95 numbers you provided.

Vivek — I'll loop you into the invite and an internal note on pricing for the Dedicated capacity test run (short-term dedicated capacity for the validation).

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@finco.com>

Quick note on pricing and capacity for the validation:

- For the 3-hour dedicated validation window (including short warm-up runs), we recommend provisioning a small Dedicated cluster (2 x A100 equivalent) to get representative latency characteristics for 16k contexts with streaming. Estimated one-time validation fee: $4,500 (covers reserved capacity + engineering time for the run + report).
- If you prefer, we can run on Hosted with a best-effort slot, but tail latencies for 16k runs may not be representative of a Dedicated deployment.

Marissa / Neha — please confirm and I'll include the cost in the calendar invite and send a draft PO template.

-Vivek
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@finco.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Alex Li <alex.li@finco.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance / SLO qualification follow-up (context window & latency)

Vivek,

We're okay with the Dedicated validation and the one-time fee. Please go ahead and add the cost to the invite; we'll route the PO through procurement once we get the run report and recommendations.

A couple of final answers to Marissa's questions:
- The 16k cases include the full customer history in ~30% of sessions; for the rest we do client-side summarization. Please model the workload mix as 70% trimmed (1k) / 30% full (16k).
- We do enforce per-user rate limits (1 req / sec) and typical token-per-minute per user is ~2,500 tokens for power users.

Sarah
